Without the 33 °C result, every bar fits the hypothesis.

n.a: 52 s is the longest time, which the hypothesis expects at the coolest temperature tested, where the enzyme should be slowest.
n.b: 44 s is shorter than at 21 °C, so the enzyme sped up as temperature rose, as predicted.
n.c: 35 s is shorter than at 25 °C, continuing the predicted speed-up below 37 °C.
n.e: 20 s is the shortest time, the fastest rate, exactly where the hypothesis places the peak.
n.f: The time rises above 37 °C, which the hypothesis predicts. A longer time here is consistent, not inconsistent.
n.g: 38 s is longer than at 41 °C, so the enzyme keeps slowing above 37 °C, as predicted.

S.q: Two healthy adults have very different natural skin tones. Which difference between their skin best explains this?
o: The amount of melanin their melanocytes produce
The number of melanocytes in their stratum corneum
The number of melanocytes in their stratum basale
The amount of keratin made by their keratinocytes
S.w: People have similar numbers of melanocytes; differences in natural skin color come mainly from how much melanin those melanocytes produce (with smaller contributions from carotene and hemoglobin).

n.1: Melanocytes are located in the stratum basale, not the dead stratum corneum.
n.2: Melanocyte numbers are similar between people; it is their melanin output that differs.
n.3: Keratin is a structural, waterproofing protein, not the main pigment behind skin tone.

S.q: A finger touches a hot pan and the arm pulls away before the person feels pain. Place the parts of this reflex arc in the order the signal passes through them, starting with the first.
o: Motor neuron
Interneuron in the spinal cord
Sensory neuron
Flexor muscle of the arm
Pain receptor in the skin
S.w: A reflex arc runs receptor, sensory neuron, integration center, motor neuron, effector. The pain receptor in the skin detects the heat, the sensory neuron carries the signal to the spinal cord, an interneuron integrates it, the motor neuron carries the command out and the flexor muscle (effector) pulls the arm away.

S.q: The DNA double helix has the same width along its entire length. Which feature of base pairing explains this uniform width?
o: Each base pair joins a purine with a pyrimidine.
Adenine pairs with guanine, both double-ring bases.
Each base pair joins two single-ring pyrimidines.
Each base pair joins two double-ring purines.
S.w: Every pair joins a double-ring purine (A or G) with a single-ring pyrimidine (T or C), so each rung of the ladder is the same width.

n.1: Adenine pairs with thymine, not guanine; A-G pairing is a common error.
n.2: Two pyrimidines would make a pair narrower; each pair contains one purine.
n.3: Two purines would make a pair wider than the others; A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

S.q: A drug overdose depresses the brain region containing the vital centers that set heart rate, breathing rhythm and blood pressure. Which region is this?
o: Primary motor cortex
Hypothalamus
Cerebellum
Medulla oblongata
S.w: The medulla oblongata of the brainstem contains the vital centers for heart rate, breathing rhythm and blood pressure, as well as reflexes such as coughing and swallowing.

n.0: The primary motor cortex in the frontal lobe controls voluntary movement, not heart rate or breathing rhythm.
n.1: The hypothalamus regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst and water balance; the vital centers are in the medulla oblongata.
n.2: The cerebellum coordinates movement, balance and posture; it does not contain the vital centers.

S.q: A website claims that an herbal tea shortens colds. It cites a celebrity endorsement and reviews from 12 happy customers. Which additional evidence would most strengthen the claim?
o: A randomized trial comparing the tea with a look-alike placebo tea
A survey finding that tea buyers report shorter colds than nonbuyers
A trial in which 300 people with colds all drank the tea and got better
A statement from a physician who recommends the tea to her patients
S.w: Only a controlled experiment can establish cause and effect. Randomly assigning people with colds to the tea or a look-alike placebo makes the groups alike except for the tea, so a difference in cold length can be credited to it.

n.1: A survey is observational: buyers chose the tea themselves and self-report their colds, so it shows an association at best, not cause.
n.2: With no comparison group, there is no way to tell whether the colds would have ended just as fast without the tea.
n.3: An authority's recommendation is not evidence; the claim still has to be tested against a control.

S.q: A nursing student is reviewing epithelial tissue before an exam. Which statements about epithelial tissue are accurate? Select all that apply.
o: It is the most abundant tissue type in the body
It rests on a basement membrane
Capillaries run between its tightly packed cells
It is nourished by diffusion from underlying tissue
Its cells regenerate rapidly after injury
Its cells are scattered in an extracellular matrix
S.w: Epithelium sits on a basement membrane, is avascular (fed by diffusion from the connective tissue beneath) and has a high capacity for regeneration.

n.0: Connective tissue is the most abundant and widespread tissue type.
n.2: Epithelium is avascular; its capillaries lie in the underlying connective tissue.
n.5: Cells scattered in an extracellular matrix describe connective tissue; epithelial cells are tightly packed.

S.q: Which observation provides the strongest support for the hypothesis that mitochondria descended from prokaryotes engulfed by an ancestral cell?
o: They have their own circular DNA and a double membrane.
They produce most of the ATP made by the cell.
They are found in plant cells as well as animal cells.
They are more numerous in muscle cells than in skin cells.
S.w: Endosymbiotic theory is supported by features mitochondria share with bacteria: their own circular DNA and ribosomes, a double membrane, and division by binary fission.

n.1: Producing most of the ATP is the function of mitochondria, not evidence of where they came from.
n.2: Being present in plants and animals is true, but it says nothing about a prokaryotic origin.
n.3: Higher numbers in active cells reflect energy demand, not ancestry.

S.q: A student balances the equation H₂ + O₂ → H₂O by rewriting the product as H₂O₂, so that each side has two oxygen atoms. Why is this method incorrect?
o: The product needs more hydrogen atoms rather than oxygen
Changing a subscript changes the identity of the substance
Hydrogen and oxygen must appear in a 1:1 ratio as products
The coefficients must be equal on both sides of the arrow
S.w: Equations are balanced with coefficients only. Changing a subscript changes the substance itself: H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide, not water. The correct balanced equation is 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O.

n.0: The product does need more oxygen, but the fix is a coefficient (2 H₂O), not changing the formula of the product.
n.2: Water has a 2:1 ratio of hydrogen to oxygen; a 1:1 ratio is exactly what turns water into hydrogen peroxide.
n.3: Coefficients do not have to match across the arrow; atom counts must. In 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O the coefficients total 3 on the left and 2 on the right.

S.q: When acidic chyme enters the duodenum, a hormone is released that signals the pancreas to secrete a fluid rich in bicarbonate. Which hormone sends this signal?
o: Secretin
Glucagon
Cholecystokinin
Gastrin
S.w: Secretin from the duodenum causes the pancreas to release bicarbonate, which neutralizes acid chyme arriving from the stomach.

n.1: Glucagon is an islet hormone that raises blood glucose and does not control bicarbonate.
n.2: Cholecystokinin mainly triggers pancreatic enzyme release and gallbladder contraction.
n.3: Gastrin is a stomach hormone that increases acid secretion, the opposite of neutralizing it.

S.q: Lithium, sodium, potassium and rubidium are all in group 1 of the periodic table. Which of these elements has the largest atomic radius, and what is the reason?
o: Rubidium, because it has the most occupied electron shells
Lithium, because it has the fewest protons pulling inward
Rubidium, because its nucleus pulls hardest on its electrons
Rubidium, because it has the most valence electrons
S.w: Atomic radius increases down a group because each element down the column adds another occupied electron shell, placing the outer electrons farther from the nucleus. Rubidium, lowest of the four, is largest.

n.1: Lithium is the smallest of the four. Having fewer protons does not outweigh having fewer shells.
n.2: Rubidium is largest, but because of its extra shells; its outer electron is actually held less tightly than in the smaller atoms.
n.3: All group 1 elements have the same number of valence electrons (one), so valence count cannot explain the size difference.

S.q: In a resting skeletal muscle fiber, most of the calcium that will trigger the next contraction is stored in which structure?
o: Sarcolemma
Sarcoplasmic reticulum
Transverse (T) tubules
Mitochondria
S.w: The sarcoplasmic reticulum, the muscle fiber's smooth ER, stores Ca²⁺ and releases it when an action potential arrives; during relaxation the Ca²⁺ is pumped back in using ATP.

n.0: The sarcolemma is the muscle cell membrane that conducts the action potential; it is not the internal calcium store.
n.2: T-tubules carry the action potential deep into the fiber; they do not store the calcium.
n.3: Mitochondria produce ATP by aerobic respiration; they are not the calcium store that triggers contraction.

S.q: Why does the electrical impulse pause briefly at the atrioventricular (AV) node before passing to the ventricles?
o: To let the atria refill with blood before they contract again
To let the SA node reset before it fires the next impulse
To let the semilunar valves close before the atria contract
To let the ventricles fill with blood before they contract
S.w: The AV node delay gives the atria time to finish contracting and push blood into the ventricles, so the ventricles are full before they contract.

n.0: The atria refill during ventricular systole and diastole; the AV delay serves ventricular filling.
n.1: The SA node's timing does not depend on the AV node delay; the delay is about ventricular filling.
n.2: The semilunar valves close at the end of ventricular systole, not before atrial contraction.

S.q: Electronegativity is a measure of how strongly an atom attracts the shared electrons in a chemical bond. Which of these elements has the highest electronegativity?
o: Fluorine
Iodine
Oxygen
Francium
S.w: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group, so it is highest at the upper right of the table (excluding noble gases). Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

n.1: Iodine is a halogen, but it sits far down group 17; electronegativity decreases down a group.
n.2: Oxygen is highly electronegative but lies one place left of fluorine in period 2, so it is slightly lower.
n.3: Francium, at the lower left of the table, has one of the lowest electronegativities of all elements.

S.q: Carbon dioxide entering the blood at the tissues is rapidly combined with water to form carbonic acid, which then releases bicarbonate. Where does the enzyme that speeds this reaction act?
o: Carbonic anhydrase inside red blood cells
Carbonic anhydrase dissolved in the plasma
Surfactant lining the alveolar walls
Hemoglobin inside the red blood cells
S.w: Carbonic anhydrase inside red blood cells catalyzes CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃. Carbonic acid releases H⁺ and HCO₃⁻, and most of the bicarbonate then moves out into the plasma for transport.

n.1: The bicarbonate ends up mostly in plasma, but the enzyme that makes it works inside red blood cells.
n.2: Surfactant lowers alveolar surface tension and is not an enzyme for CO₂ conversion.
n.3: Hemoglobin carries O₂ and some CO₂ and buffers H⁺, but it is not the enzyme that forms carbonic acid.

S.q: Under a microscope, a student estimates that a rod-shaped bacterium is 0.0000032 m long. How is this length written in scientific notation?
S.w: Move the decimal point right until one nonzero digit is in front of it: 0.0000032 becomes 3.2 after 6 moves. A number less than 1 takes a negative exponent, so the length is 3.2 × 10⁻⁶ m.

n.1: This counts 5 decimal moves instead of 6; 3.2 × 10⁻⁵ equals 0.000032.
n.2: A positive exponent describes a number greater than 1 (3,200,000), not a tiny length.
n.3: The value is equal, but the coefficient 32 is not between 1 and 10, so it is not proper scientific notation.

S.q: A poison control leaflet explains that a few substances can enter the blood directly through the stomach lining, before reaching the small intestine. Which substance is one of these?
o: Alcohol
Vitamin B12
Fatty acids
Amino acids
S.w: The stomach absorbs very little, but some water, alcohol and aspirin can cross its lining. Nutrients are absorbed mainly in the small intestine.

n.1: Vitamin B12 is absorbed in the ileum with intrinsic factor, not across the stomach lining.
n.2: Fatty acids are absorbed in the small intestine and enter the lacteals as chylomicrons.
n.3: Amino acids are absorbed into blood capillaries of the small intestine villi.

S.q: A 64-year-old woman is diagnosed with osteoporosis several years after menopause. Which change in bone remodeling best accounts for her loss of bone mass?
o: Osteoblast formation outpaces osteoclast resorption
Osteoclast resorption outpaces osteoblast formation
Calcitonin rises and stimulates osteoclast resorption
Osteoblasts resorb more matrix as estrogen declines
S.w: Bone is constantly remodeled by osteoblasts (which build) and osteoclasts (which resorb). After menopause estrogen falls, resorption exceeds formation, and bone mass is lost: osteoporosis.

n.0: If formation outpaced resorption, bone mass would increase rather than decrease.
n.2: Calcitonin lowers blood calcium by inhibiting osteoclasts; it does not stimulate bone resorption.
n.3: Osteoblasts build bone; resorbing matrix is the job of osteoclasts.

S.q: A patient is told to chew an antacid tablet thoroughly rather than swallow it whole so it neutralizes stomach acid faster. Which factor explains the faster reaction?
o: Greater surface area of the tablet exposed to acid
Higher concentration of the antacid in each particle
Lower activation energy for each antacid particle
Higher temperature produced by the act of chewing
S.w: Breaking a solid into small pieces exposes more of its particles to the other reactant, increasing the number of collisions per second. Greater surface area increases the reaction rate.

n.1: Chewing breaks the tablet into smaller pieces but does not change the concentration of antacid within each piece.
n.2: Chewing does not change the reaction pathway, so the activation energy stays the same; only a catalyst lowers it.
n.3: Chewing does not noticeably warm the tablet; the effect comes from the increased surface area.

S.q: A student hypothesizes that the concentration of a drug in the blood one hour after a dose is directly proportional to the dose. The bar graph shows the results. Select the bar that is inconsistent with this hypothesis.
S.w: If the level is directly proportional to the dose, level / dose is the same for every bar: 4/50 = 8/100 = 12/150 = 16/200 = 24/300 = 0.08. For 250 mg the hypothesis predicts 0.08 x 250 = 20, but the bar shows 22, so it does not fit.

n.a: 4 / 50 = 0.08, the same ratio as the other matching bars.
n.b: 8 / 100 = 0.08. Doubling the dose from 50 mg doubled the level, as direct proportion predicts.
n.f: 24 is the tallest bar, and the step up from 22 is small, but 24 / 300 = 0.08 fits. The small step happens because the 250 mg bar is too high.

S.q: A runner moves from sea level to train at high altitude for two months. Place the events in the order they occur as her body adjusts, starting with the first.
o: The kidneys detect a low blood oxygen level
The blood's oxygen-carrying capacity rises over weeks
The kidneys release erythropoietin (EPO)
Red bone marrow increases red blood cell production
Less oxygen reaches the blood from the thinner air
S.w: High altitude means less oxygen enters the blood. The kidneys sense the low oxygen and release EPO, a hormone that signals red bone marrow to make more red blood cells. Over weeks, the extra red blood cells raise the blood's capacity to carry oxygen.

S.q: A student compares two tomato plants. Plant A gets fertilizer and sits in a sunny window; Plant B gets no fertilizer and sits in a shaded hallway. Plant A grows taller. What is the main flaw in this design?
o: Two variables differ, so the cause is unclear.
Plant height should be plotted on the x-axis.
The dependent variable should be fertilizer.
There is no control group to compare against.
S.w: A fair test changes one variable at a time. Fertilizer and light both differ, so the extra growth cannot be credited to fertilizer; light could explain it.

n.1: Height is the dependent variable, which belongs on the y-axis.
n.2: Fertilizer is what the student changes, so it is the independent variable, not the dependent variable.
n.3: Plant B, with no fertilizer, is meant as the comparison; the problem is that it also differs in light.

S.q: A soccer player straightens the knee forcefully to kick a ball. Which muscle group is the prime mover for this knee movement?
o: Quadriceps femoris
Gastrocnemius and soleus
Gluteus maximus
Hamstring muscles
S.w: Straightening the knee is extension, and the quadriceps femoris (including the rectus femoris and vastus lateralis) is the prime mover of knee extension.

n.1: The gastrocnemius and soleus plantar flex the ankle; they do not extend the knee.
n.2: The gluteus maximus extends the hip; it does not cross the knee to straighten it.
n.3: The hamstrings flex the knee and extend the hip; they oppose knee extension.

S.q: A cross between a red-haired bull and a white-haired cow produces roan calves, whose coats contain a mixture of separate red hairs and white hairs. Which pattern of inheritance explains the roan coat?
o: Incomplete dominance
Multiple alleles
Sex-linked inheritance
Codominance
S.w: In codominance both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote; roan cattle show both red hairs and white hairs side by side.

n.0: Incomplete dominance would give a single blended color (for example, pink hairs), not separate red and white hairs.
n.1: Multiple alleles means more than two alleles in the population; only two (red and white) are involved here.
n.2: Coat color here is inherited the same way in both sexes; the cross does not involve a sex-chromosome pattern.

S.q: Place these substances in order of pH, starting with the most acidic and ending with the most basic.
o: Household ammonia
Stomach acid
Black coffee
Human blood
Pure water
S.w: Approximate pH values: stomach acid 1.5-3.5, black coffee about 5, pure water 7 (neutral), blood 7.35-7.45 (slightly basic) and household ammonia about 11. Lower pH means more acidic.

S.q: A patient with lactose intolerance makes too little lactase. When lactase does digest lactose, which two monosaccharides are released?
o: Glucose and galactose
Galactose and fructose
Glucose and glucose
Glucose and fructose
S.w: Lactose (milk sugar) = glucose + galactose. Lactase hydrolyzes it into those two monosaccharides.

n.1: Galactose + fructose is not one of the common dietary disaccharides.
n.2: Glucose + glucose make maltose.
n.3: Glucose + fructose make sucrose (table sugar).

S.q: Pasta takes longer to cook in boiling water in Denver, Colorado (elevation about 5,280 feet) than in Miami, Florida, near sea level. What explains this difference?
o: Colder air at high altitude removes heat from the pot more quickly
Thinner air holds less oxygen, which lowers water's boiling point
Lower air pressure at high altitude lowers water's boiling point
Higher air pressure at high altitude slows the escape of molecules
S.w: A liquid boils when its vapor pressure equals the surrounding pressure. At high altitude, air pressure is lower, so water boils at a lower temperature (below 100 °C). The boiling water is cooler, so food cooks more slowly.

n.0: Once water boils, its temperature is set by the boiling point, not by the outside air temperature.
n.1: The boiling point is lower at altitude, but the cause is lower air pressure; the oxygen content of the air does not set the boiling point of water.
n.3: Air pressure is lower, not higher, at high altitude. Higher pressure (as in a pressure cooker) raises the boiling point.

S.q: Blood enters each glomerulus through one arteriole and leaves through another. Which vessel delivers blood into the glomerulus?
o: Efferent arteriole
Peritubular capillary
Afferent arteriole
Renal vein
S.w: The afferent arteriole carries blood into the glomerulus; the efferent arteriole carries it out to the peritubular capillaries. (Afferent = arrives; efferent = exits.)

n.0: The efferent arteriole carries blood out of the glomerulus, not into it.
n.1: Peritubular capillaries receive blood from the efferent arteriole after it leaves the glomerulus.
n.3: Veins drain blood away from the kidney tissue; they do not supply the glomerulus.

S.q: A home pregnancy test detects a hormone in urine shortly after a blastocyst implants. Which statement correctly identifies this hormone and its role in early pregnancy?
o: hCG from the mother's anterior pituitary, which keeps the corpus luteum alive
Progesterone from the corpus luteum, which keeps the endometrium intact
hCG from the embryo's trophoblast, which keeps the corpus luteum alive
LH from the mother's anterior pituitary, which triggers implantation
S.w: Pregnancy tests detect hCG, secreted by the trophoblast of the implanted blastocyst (later the placenta). hCG keeps the corpus luteum alive so it keeps secreting progesterone, which maintains the endometrium.

n.0: hCG is made by the embryo's trophoblast, not by the mother's pituitary.
n.1: Progesterone does maintain the endometrium, but home pregnancy tests detect hCG, not progesterone.
n.3: LH triggers ovulation, not implantation, and it is not the hormone pregnancy tests detect.

S.q: A student checks four chemical equations for a lab report. Which of these equations is correctly balanced?
o: 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O
N₂ + 3 H₂ → NH₃
2 Na + Cl₂ → NaCl
CH₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + 2 H₂O
S.w: In 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O, each side has 4 H atoms and 2 O atoms, so the equation is balanced.

n.1: The left side has 2 N and 6 H, the right has 1 N and 3 H; the balanced form is N₂ + 3 H₂ → 2 NH₃.
n.2: The left side has 2 Na and 2 Cl, the right has 1 of each; the balanced form is 2 Na + Cl₂ → 2 NaCl.
n.3: The left side has 2 O atoms and the right has 4 (2 in CO₂ and 2 in 2 H₂O); the balanced form is CH₄ + 2 O₂ → CO₂ + 2 H₂O.

S.q: Directional terms in anatomy are defined relative to anatomical position. Which description matches anatomical position?
o: Lying face up, arms at the sides, palms facing up, feet pointing forward
Standing upright, facing forward, arms at the sides, palms facing forward
Standing upright, facing forward, arms raised, palms facing forward
Standing upright, facing forward, arms at the sides, palms facing the thighs
S.w: In anatomical position the body is upright and facing forward, feet flat and pointing forward, arms at the sides, palms facing forward (anterior) with the thumbs pointing away from the body.

n.0: Lying face up is the supine position. Anatomical position is upright.
n.2: The arms hang at the sides in anatomical position; they are not raised.
n.3: Palms facing the thighs is a relaxed standing posture. In anatomical position the palms face forward.

S.q: A class measures how fast an enzyme breaks down hydrogen peroxide at 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 °C. How should the axes of their graph be labeled?
o: Enzyme activity on the x-axis; temperature on the y-axis
Time on the x-axis; temperature on the y-axis
Time on the x-axis; enzyme activity on the y-axis
Temperature on the x-axis; enzyme activity on the y-axis
S.w: The independent variable (temperature, which the class sets) goes on the x-axis, and the dependent variable (enzyme activity, which is measured) goes on the y-axis.

n.0: This places the dependent variable on the x-axis; it belongs on the y-axis.
n.1: This leaves the dependent variable, enzyme activity, off the graph.
n.2: Time is not the variable the class changed; temperature is the independent variable here.

S.q: Cardiac muscle is autorhythmic. Which statement best describes the role of the autonomic nervous system in heart rate?
o: It sets the rhythm: the medulla sends one impulse to the ventricles per beat
It adjusts the rate: sympathetic nerves speed it and the vagus nerve slows it
It adjusts the rate: the vagus nerve speeds it and sympathetic nerves slow it
It starts each beat: sympathetic nerves fire the SA node with each heartbeat
S.w: The SA node generates each beat without nerve input. The autonomic nervous system only changes the rate: sympathetic stimulation speeds it up and parasympathetic (vagus) stimulation slows it.

n.0: The medulla's cardiac center adjusts autonomic output, but the impulse for each beat comes from the SA node.
n.2: The roles are reversed: the vagus (parasympathetic) slows the heart and sympathetic nerves speed it.
n.3: The SA node fires on its own (autorhythmicity); nerves modify the rate but do not trigger each beat.

S.q: A toxin blocks the electron transport chain in a patient's cells. Which change in those cells would be expected?
o: Glucose is broken down directly into CO₂ in the cytoplasm.
Oxygen use rises, as more is needed to accept electrons.
ATP output rises, as glycolysis no longer competes for glucose.
ATP output drops, and cells shift to lactic acid fermentation.
S.w: Step 1: the electron transport chain makes most of the cell's ATP, so blocking it causes a sharp fall in ATP. Step 2: cells fall back on glycolysis, which needs no oxygen, regenerating its needs by lactic acid fermentation.

n.0: CO₂ is released in the mitochondria (pyruvate oxidation and Krebs cycle), not from glucose in the cytoplasm.
n.1: Oxygen is used only as the final electron acceptor of the chain, so a blocked chain uses less oxygen, not more.
n.2: Glycolysis makes only 2 ATP per glucose, so losing the chain lowers ATP output; it does not raise it.

S.q: A textbook describes the two strands of a DNA double helix as antiparallel. What does this term mean?
o: The two strands run in opposite directions.
One strand is made of DNA and the other of RNA.
The strands are joined by covalent bonds between bases.
The two strands have exactly the same base sequence.
S.w: Antiparallel means the two strands run in opposite directions: one runs 5' to 3' and its partner runs 3' to 5'.

n.1: Both strands of the double helix are DNA. DNA-RNA pairing happens only briefly during transcription.
n.2: Bases are joined across the strands by hydrogen bonds; that describes bonding, not direction.
n.3: The strands are complementary (A-T, G-C), not identical in sequence.

S.q: Throughout a lab, a student reads the water level in each graduated cylinder while standing and looking down at the meniscus. Which statement describes the effect on the volume data?
o: The error spreads out the readings but leaves their mean accurate.
The readings become more precise because the angle is the same each time.
Readings shift the same way each time, so averaging will not remove the error.
Readings scatter in both directions, so averaging trials removes the error.
S.w: Reading from above (parallax) shifts every reading in the same direction, which is systematic error. It reduces accuracy, and averaging repeated trials cannot cancel an error that always points the same way.

n.0: Parallax from a fixed angle moves the mean away from the true value, so the mean is not accurate.
n.1: Readings can agree with one another and still be wrong; the consistent angle produces a bias, not improved quality.
n.3: This describes random error; a consistent viewing angle produces a consistent shift, not scatter.

S.q: A science teacher lists four well-established statements on the board. Which statement is best classified as a scientific theory rather than a scientific law?
o: At constant temperature, a gas's pressure varies inversely with its volume.
In a closed system, total mass is the same before and after a reaction.
Two masses attract with a force that depends on their masses and distance.
All living things are made of cells, and new cells come from existing cells.
S.w: Cell theory is a broad explanation of how living things are organized and reproduce, supported by many observations. The other statements describe consistent, often mathematical, patterns without explaining why, which is what laws do.

n.0: This is Boyle's law, a mathematical description of a pattern in gases.
n.1: This is the law of conservation of mass: a description of what always happens in reactions.
n.2: This is the law of gravitation, a mathematical description of the attraction between masses.

S.q: Before giving an injection, a nurse cleans the patient's skin with an alcohol-based solution to reduce the number of microbes. What is this practice called?
o: Sterilization
Antisepsis
Disinfection
Pasteurization
S.w: Antisepsis reduces microbes on living tissue such as skin. Disinfection is for objects and surfaces.

n.0: Sterilization kills all microbes including endospores (as in an autoclave) and is not done on skin.
n.2: Disinfection reduces pathogens on objects and surfaces, not on living tissue.
n.3: Pasteurization is gentle heating of foods such as milk, not skin preparation.

S.q: A patient stops taking a prescribed antibiotic after three days because she feels better. Why can this practice contribute to antibiotic resistance?
o: The drug makes each bacterium change to resist it.
Her body itself becomes resistant to the antibiotic.
Viruses in her body learn to resist antibiotics.
Surviving bacteria tend to be the most resistant ones.
S.w: An incomplete course kills the most susceptible bacteria first; the survivors are more likely to carry resistance, and they multiply. This is natural selection, and resistance genes can also spread on plasmids.

n.0: Antibiotics do not make bacteria change on purpose; they select bacteria that already carry resistance.
n.1: Resistance is a property of the bacteria, not of the patient's body.
n.2: Antibiotics do not act on viruses, so viral resistance to them is not the issue.

S.q: In a classroom demonstration, a chicken bone is soaked in vinegar until its mineral salts dissolve. The bone keeps its shape but can now be bent easily. Which matrix component remains and gives this flexibility?
o: Collagen fibers
Osteocytes within lacunae
Elastin fibers
Calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite)
S.w: Bone matrix is about one-third organic, mostly collagen (flexibility and tensile strength), and two-thirds inorganic calcium phosphate as hydroxyapatite (hardness). Acid dissolves the mineral and leaves the collagen framework, so the bone bends.

n.1: Osteocytes maintain the matrix but are cells, not the fibrous part of the matrix that resists bending forces.
n.2: Elastin gives stretch and recoil in skin and elastic cartilage; the organic fiber of bone matrix is collagen.
n.3: Hydroxyapatite gives bone its hardness and is the part the acid dissolves; once it is gone the bone loses rigidity.

S.q: To slow preterm labor, a patient is given a drug that blocks oxytocin receptors in the uterus. The activity of which part of the uterus is this drug intended to reduce?
o: Myometrium, the smooth muscle layer
Cervix, the narrow lower neck
Endometrium, the glandular lining
Perimetrium, the outer serous layer
S.w: Two steps. (1) Oxytocin from the posterior pituitary stimulates uterine contractions in labor. (2) Those contractions come from the myometrium, the smooth muscle layer of the uterine wall. Blocking oxytocin receptors aims to quiet the myometrium.

n.1: The cervix is the lower neck that opens into the vagina; the contractions oxytocin drives come from the myometrium of the uterine wall.
n.2: The endometrium is the lining where implantation occurs and that is shed in menstruation; it does not generate labor contractions.
n.3: The perimetrium is the thin outer covering of the uterus; it does not produce the contractions of labor.

S.q: Butter is solid at room temperature, while olive oil is liquid. Which difference in their fatty acids best explains this?
o: Butter's fats contain more glycerol molecules per fatty acid.
Olive oil's fatty acids carry more hydrogen atoms per carbon.
Butter's fatty acids are mostly saturated and pack tightly together.
Butter's fatty acids have more C=C double bonds, which form kinks.
S.w: Saturated fatty acids have no C=C double bonds, so their straight chains pack tightly and the fat is solid. Unsaturated fatty acids in oils have double bonds that kink the chains.

n.0: Every triglyceride has one glycerol and three fatty acids; the difference is saturation.
n.1: This is reversed: saturated fatty acids such as butter's carry the most hydrogen. Olive oil's C=C double bonds mean fewer hydrogens.
n.3: This is reversed: double bonds and kinks belong to unsaturated fats, which are liquid.

S.q: A routine blood test shows that a patient's calcium level has dropped below its normal range. Which responses would be expected as the body restores it? Select all that apply.
o: Increased secretion of parathyroid hormone
Increased loss of calcium from the kidneys into the urine
Increased deposition of calcium into the bone matrix
More active vitamin D, so the gut absorbs more calcium
Increased calcitonin secretion from the thyroid C cells
Increased osteoclast activity releasing calcium from bone
S.w: Low blood calcium triggers PTH release. PTH stimulates osteoclasts to release calcium from bone, makes the kidneys keep calcium and activates vitamin D so the gut absorbs more calcium.

n.1: PTH makes the kidneys keep calcium, so urinary calcium loss would fall, not rise.
n.2: Depositing calcium into bone lowers blood calcium; that is the calcitonin response to high calcium.
n.4: Calcitonin is released when blood calcium is high and lowers it, so its secretion would fall.

S.q: A beaker of crushed ice at 0 °C is heated steadily on a hot plate. While the ice is melting and some solid is still present, what happens to the temperature of the ice-water mixture?
o: It stays at 0 °C, because the energy breaks attractions between molecules
It rises to 4 °C, where water is densest, before melting is complete
It rises steadily, because the heat raises the molecules' kinetic energy
It falls slightly, because melting releases heat to the surroundings
S.w: During a phase change, the temperature stays constant. The added energy (heat of fusion) goes into breaking the attractions holding molecules in the solid, not into raising their average kinetic energy. This is the flat plateau on a heating curve.

n.1: Water is densest at about 4 °C, but the mixture does not warm above 0 °C until all the ice has melted.
n.2: The temperature rises before and after melting, but not during it; the energy is used to change the state.
n.3: Melting absorbs heat (endothermic). Freezing is the change that releases heat.

S.q: A student tests four liquids with a simple conductivity tester that lights a bulb when current flows. Which liquid will light the bulb?
o: Table sugar (sucrose) dissolved in water
Pure distilled water
Ethanol mixed with an equal volume of water
Potassium chloride dissolved in water
S.w: Ionic compounds such as KCl dissociate into ions (K+ and Cl⁻) in water. Mobile ions carry current, so the solution is an electrolyte and conducts electricity.

n.0: Sucrose dissolves as whole molecules, not ions, so its solution is a nonelectrolyte.
n.1: Pure water contains too few ions to conduct noticeably; dissolved ions are what make tap and salt water conduct.
n.2: Ethanol dissolves as neutral molecules, so the mixture does not conduct.

S.q: Which glands secrete an oily substance, usually into hair follicles, that softens skin and hair, slows water loss and helps inhibit bacterial growth?
o: Sebaceous glands
Ceruminous glands
Apocrine sweat glands
Eccrine sweat glands
S.w: Sebaceous (oil) glands secrete sebum, usually into hair follicles. Sebum lubricates and softens skin and hair, slows water loss and is antibacterial. They are absent from the palms and soles.

n.1: Ceruminous glands are modified sweat glands that produce earwax in the ear canal.
n.2: Apocrine glands also open into hair follicles, but they secrete a thicker sweat, not oily sebum.
n.3: Eccrine glands open onto the skin surface through pores and secrete watery sweat.

S.q: A hiker climbs to high altitude, where each breath holds less oxygen. Which receptors respond most directly to the drop in blood oxygen?
o: Central chemoreceptors on the surface of the medulla oblongata
Peripheral chemoreceptors in the carotid and aortic bodies
Stretch receptors in the walls of the bronchioles
Baroreceptors in the carotid sinus and the aortic arch
S.w: Peripheral chemoreceptors in the carotid and aortic bodies respond to low O₂ (and also to CO₂ and H⁺), signaling the medulla to increase ventilation.

n.0: Central chemoreceptors respond to CO₂ through the pH of cerebrospinal fluid, not to low oxygen.
n.2: Bronchiolar stretch receptors sense lung inflation, not blood oxygen.
n.3: Baroreceptors sense stretch from blood pressure, not oxygen levels.

S.q: A black guinea pig, where black (B) is dominant over white (b), is crossed with a white guinea pig. The litter has 5 black and 4 white pups. What is the genotype of the black parent?
o: bb, because white pups appeared in the litter
BB, because black is the dominant allele
BB, because most of the pups are black
Bb, because some of the pups are white
S.w: Step 1: a white pup is bb and must get b from each parent. Step 2: the black parent therefore carries b, so it is Bb. The roughly 1:1 ratio matches the Bb x bb test cross.

n.0: A bb parent would itself be white, but this parent is black.
n.1: Black being dominant tells you the parent has at least one B, not that it has two.
n.2: A BB parent could pass on only B, so every pup would be black; the white pups rule this out.

S.q: A student records the mass of a tiny crystal as 0.004050 g on an analytical balance. How many significant figures does this measurement contain?
S.w: Leading zeros (0.00) are placeholders and never count. The 4 and 5 count, the zero between them counts, and the trailing zero after the decimal point counts: 4, 0, 5, 0 = 4 significant figures.

n.0: This counts the zeros after the decimal point that come before the 4; leading zeros are not significant.
n.1: This drops the final zero; a trailing zero to the right of a decimal point is significant.
n.3: This counts every digit written, including all the leading zeros.

S.q: Both B and T lymphocytes arise from stem cells in red bone marrow. Where does each type of lymphocyte complete its maturation before it can respond to antigens?
o: T cells in the thymus; B cells in red bone marrow
T cells in the lymph nodes; B cells in red bone marrow
T cells in the thymus; B cells in the spleen
T cells in red bone marrow; B cells in the thymus
S.w: T cells mature in the thymus (T for thymus), and B cells mature in red bone marrow. These are the two primary lymphoid organs.

n.1: Lymph nodes are secondary lymphoid organs that house mature lymphocytes; T cells mature in the thymus.
n.2: The spleen is a secondary lymphoid organ where mature lymphocytes respond to antigens; B cells mature in red bone marrow.
n.3: This reverses the two sites: T cells mature in the thymus and B cells in red bone marrow.

E.q: The pharmacist reassured the patient that the drug's side effects are reversible once the medication is stopped. Based on its root, what does reversible mean?
o: Able to be sent back
Able to be pulled back
Able to be turned back
Able to be built again
E.w: re- means back or again, the root vers means turn, and -ible means able to be, so reversible means able to be turned back (undone).

n.0: Sending is the meaning of mit/mis (as in remission or transmit), not vers.
n.1: Pulling is the meaning of tract (as in retract), not vers.
n.3: Building is the meaning of struct (as in reconstruct).

E.q: A receptionist is recording a phone call. Which sentence uses end punctuation correctly?
o: The patient asked, "Whether the clinic would be open on Monday?"
The patient asked whether the clinic would be open on Monday.
The patient asked whether the clinic would be open on Monday?
The patient asked, whether the clinic would be open on Monday.
E.w: This is an indirect question: it reports what was asked without quoting the exact words, so it ends with a period and takes no comma or quotation marks.

n.0: These are not the patient's exact words, so quotation marks are wrong.
n.2: An indirect question is a statement, so it ends with a period, not a question mark.
n.3: No comma separates the verb "asked" from the clause that is its object.

E.q: Ellen's working thesis is "Technology has changed health care." Her instructor says the thesis is too broad for a four-page paper. Which revision best fixes this problem?
o: Telehealth has made follow-up care easier for rural patients in Montana.
This paper will explain the ways technology has changed health care.
Has technology changed health care for the better or for the worse?
Technology has changed health care in many important ways over time.
E.w: A thesis should be narrow enough to cover in the space available. Narrowing "technology" to telehealth, "health care" to follow-up care, and the population to rural patients in one state gives a focused, arguable claim.

n.1: This is an announcement of the topic, and the topic is still as broad as the original.
n.2: Turning the thesis into a question removes the claim instead of narrowing it.
n.3: Adding "in many important ways" keeps the claim just as broad and vague.

E.q: Devon is preparing the final copy of a report on campus flu shots. Which of the following tasks belongs to the editing stage rather than the revising stage?
o: Adding a statistic to support the second main point
Fixing a pronoun that disagrees with its antecedent
Reordering paragraphs so the strongest point is last
Removing a sentence that is off topic for its paragraph
E.w: Editing deals with sentence-level correctness: grammar, usage, punctuation, spelling and consistency. A pronoun-antecedent agreement error is a grammar problem, so fixing it is editing.

n.0: Adding support changes the content of the report, which is revising (add).
n.2: Reordering paragraphs changes the organization, which is revising (rearrange).
n.3: Cutting an off-topic sentence improves unity and content, which is revising (remove).

E.q: A hospital's staff profile page is being edited. Which sentence uses verb tense correctly with the phrase "since 2019"?
o: Dr. Patel has worked at the hospital in 2019.
Dr. Patel works at the hospital since 2019.
Dr. Patel is working at the hospital since 2019.
Dr. Patel has worked at the hospital since 2019.
E.w: The present perfect (has/have + past participle) shows an action that began in the past and continues now: "has worked ... since 2019."

n.0: The present perfect does not pair with a finished, specific past time such as "in 2019"; use "worked in 2019."
n.1: "Since" marks an action that began in the past and continues, which needs the present perfect "has worked."
n.2: The present progressive does not fit an ongoing span that began at a past point; use "has worked" or "has been working."

E.q: Kenji reduces a six-page article on diabetes prevention to three sentences, in his own words, that state the article's main ideas, and he cites the article. What has Kenji written?
o: A direct quotation
A summary
A paraphrase
A reference entry
E.w: A summary gives only the main ideas of a source, in the writer's own words, and is much shorter than the original. Like a paraphrase, it must be cited.

n.0: A direct quotation reproduces the source's exact words in quotation marks; Kenji used his own words.
n.2: A paraphrase restates one specific passage at about the same length; Kenji condensed a whole article to three sentences.
n.3: A reference entry lists a source's publication details at the end of the paper; it does not restate ideas.

E.q: The lab returned the patient's sample with a note that hemolysis had occurred during collection, so the blood had to be drawn again. Based on its word parts, what does hemolysis mean?
o: Bursting forth of blood
Breakdown of blood cells
Abnormal clotting of blood
Stopping of blood flow
E.w: hem/o means blood and -lysis means breakdown or destruction, so hemolysis is the breakdown of (red) blood cells.

n.0: Bursting forth of blood (bleeding) is hemorrhage; -rrhage is the suffix.
n.2: A clot is thromb/o (thrombosis); -lysis means breakdown, the opposite of forming a clot.
n.3: Stopping blood flow is hemostasis; -stasis means stopping.

E.q: Read the excerpt from an application letter. Select the word that is too informal for the letter's audience and purpose.

parts:
Dear Admissions Committee:

Last summer, I
on the pediatric unit at Mercy Hospital, where I
who were recovering from surgery. That experience
my commitment to a career in pediatric nursing. I am writing to
my interest in the Bachelor of Science in Nursing program at Westfield University, and I would welcome the chance to discuss my application.

E.w: "Kids" is casual, conversational wording. A letter to an admissions committee calls for formal language, such as children or young patients.

n.a: "Express" is the standard formal verb for stating interest in a program.
n.b: "Volunteered" is a precise, neutral verb that suits formal writing.
n.c: "Helped" is plain, but plain is not the same as informal. It is standard in formal writing.

E.q: Which pair of words correctly completes the sentence? "By the time the team was ____ to begin, the patient had ____ been discharged."
o: all ready; already
all ready; all ready
already; all ready
already; already
E.w: "All ready" means completely prepared (the team was all ready to begin); "already" means by this time (had already been discharged).

n.1: "Had all ready been discharged" needs the time word "already".
n.2: Both are reversed: being prepared is "all ready", and "by this time" is "already".
n.3: Being completely prepared is "all ready"; "was already to begin" does not make sense.

E.q: A nurse is ending an email to her unit manager that requests a change to next month's schedule. Which closing sentence is most appropriate?
o: Let me know ASAP, since I already told my family I'd be off that weekend.
Thanks in advance for approving this change to my schedule.
Thank you for considering my request; I am glad to discuss it at any time.
I trust you will approve this request, as I have certainly earned it by now.
E.w: A professional email closes courteously, thanks the reader and offers to follow up.

n.0: "ASAP" and the assumption that the request is already approved are too informal and presumptuous.
n.1: Thanking the manager in advance "for approving" assumes the answer and pressures the reader.
n.3: The demanding tone pressures the manager and is not respectful.

E.q: A nurse is documenting how long a procedure took. Which sentence uses "than" and "then" correctly?
o: The test took longer than expected, so we ate lunch and than left.
The test took longer then expected, so we ate lunch and than left.
The test took longer then expected, so we ate lunch and then left.
The test took longer than expected, so we ate lunch and then left.
E.w: "Than" makes a comparison (longer than expected); "then" shows time or sequence (and then left).

n.0: "And ___ left" shows sequence, so it needs "then".
n.1: Both are reversed: the comparison needs "than" and the sequence needs "then".
n.2: "Longer ___ expected" is a comparison, so it needs "than".

E.q: A patient was diagnosed with hemiplegia and began a rehabilitation program with a physical therapist three times a week. Based on its word parts, what does hemiplegia mean?
o: Paralysis on one side of the body
Paralysis caused by a brain bleed
Paralysis affecting both of the legs
Paralysis of all four of the limbs
E.w: hemi- means half and -plegia means paralysis, so hemiplegia is paralysis of one half (one side) of the body.

n.1: hemi- (half) is not hem/o (blood); the word says nothing about bleeding.
n.2: Paralysis of both legs is paraplegia; hemi- refers to one side, not both legs.
n.3: Paralysis of all four limbs is quadriplegia; quadri- means four.

E.q: The hospital's quality committee reviewed mortality data from the past year to compare outcomes across its units. Based on its root, what do mortality data measure?
o: The number of diseases diagnosed
The number of deaths
The number of patients transferred
The number of births
E.w: The root mort means death, so mortality data measure deaths (for example, deaths per 1,000 patients).

n.0: Disease is the meaning of path (as in pathology).
n.2: Transfer relates to port (carry) or mit (send), not mort.
n.3: Births relate to natal (as in prenatal), not mort.

E.q: A patient satisfaction survey summary is being edited. Which sentence uses an adjective correctly after a linking verb?
o: The coffee in the staff break room tastes bitter today.
The infant is breathing good now that the fever has broken.
Their new manager seems nicely, and the staff likes her a lot.
The cafeteria food tastes differently since the new cook started.
E.w: Linking verbs (taste, seem, feel, look, smell) connect the subject to an adjective that describes it: the coffee tastes bitter.

n.1: "Breathing" is an action, so it needs the adverb "well," not the adjective "good."
n.2: "Seems" is a linking verb, so it takes the adjective "nice," not the adverb "nicely."
n.3: "Tastes" links the food to a description, so it needs the adjective "different," not the adverb.

E.q: Read the paragraph. (1) Last summer, Jamal volunteered at Mercy Hospital in Ohio. (2) He worked with a nurse named Carla Diaz. (3) Every Friday, he helped the Hospital's chaplain plan services. (4) In September, he started classes at Lakeview Community College. Which sentence contains a capitalization error?
o: Sentence 1
Sentence 2
Sentence 3
Sentence 4
E.w: In sentence 3, "hospital" is a general noun (the hospital's chaplain), not part of a name, so it should be lowercase.

n.0: "Mercy Hospital" is a proper name and "Ohio" is a state; "summer" is correctly lowercase.
n.1: "Carla Diaz" is a name, and "nurse" is correctly lowercase.
n.3: "September" is a month and "Lakeview Community College" is a proper name.

E.q: Read the paragraph. Select the transition that signals the wrong relationship between the sentences it connects.

parts: Many nursing students find pharmacology difficult.
, many drug names look and sound alike.
, the course is one of the most demanding in the program.
, students who join a study group early tend to earn higher grades.
, many instructors now assign study partners during the first week.

E.w: The sentence about study groups turns from the problem (pharmacology is hard) to a way students succeed despite it. That is a contrast, so it needs a word such as however. "Similarly" signals that the new idea is like the one before it, which it is not.

n.a: Look-alike drug names are one example of why the course is difficult, so "For example" fits.
n.b: Dosage math is a second, separate difficulty, so the addition transition fits.
n.c: The two difficulties lead to the conclusion that the course is demanding, so a cause-and-effect transition fits.
n.e: Because study groups help, instructors assign partners. The second idea results from the first, so "As a result" fits.

E.q: Read the passage. Select the word that is used incorrectly.

parts: main goal is to reduce wait times, and the front-desk staff members say
ready for the change. Visits should be shorter
they were last year, and the clinic's

E.w: The sentence needs the contraction they're (they are): the staff members say they are ready. Their is a possessive pronoun and must be followed by something the staff members own.

n.a: Affect is the verb meaning to influence. The policy will influence how patients schedule visits, so it is correct.
n.b: Its is the possessive form (the policy's main goal). It's would mean it is, which does not fit.
n.d: Than is used for comparisons (shorter than last year). Then refers to time.
n.e: Principal means main or chief, which fits. Principle means a rule or belief.

E.q: A research summary reads: "The trial drug lowered blood pressure in most participants. ___, several participants reported dizziness and headaches." Which transitions could correctly fill the blank? Select all that apply.
o: For instance
Therefore
Similarly
However
On the other hand
E.w: The second sentence presents a drawback that contrasts with the benefit in the first. "However" and "On the other hand" both signal contrast.

n.0: "For instance" introduces an example of the first sentence, but side effects are not an example of lower blood pressure.
n.1: "Therefore" signals a result, but the side effects are not a consequence of the blood pressure falling in this passage.
n.2: "Similarly" signals a matching point, but a drawback does not match a benefit.

E.q: Before the next patient's procedure, the technician cleaned and tested the endoscope according to the hospital's infection-control policy. Based on its suffix, what is an endoscope?
o: A record of images from inside the body
A surgical cut made into the body
A procedure that views inside the body
An instrument for viewing inside the body
E.w: endo- means within and -scope means an instrument for viewing, so an endoscope is the instrument used to look inside the body.

n.0: A record or image is -gram; -scope is the viewing instrument.
n.1: A surgical cut is -otomy; nothing in endoscope refers to cutting.
n.2: The procedure is endoscopy; -scopy names the examination, while -scope names the instrument.

E.q: Read the paragraph from a study-skills guide. (1) Many students believe that cramming the night before an exam is effective. (2) Therefore, research shows that spacing study sessions over several days leads to better recall. (3) For example, students who reviewed material on four separate days remembered more a week later. (4) Overall, spaced practice is a better use of study time than cramming. Which sentence uses an illogical transition?
o: Sentence 2
Sentence 4
Sentence 3
Sentence 1
E.w: Sentence 2 contradicts the belief in sentence 1, so it needs a contrast transition such as "However," not the cause-and-effect "Therefore."

n.1: "Overall" correctly signals a summary of the paragraph's point.
n.2: "For example" correctly introduces a specific study that illustrates sentence 2.
n.3: Sentence 1 has no transition; it introduces the belief the paragraph will challenge.

E.q: A student is editing a peer's care-plan summary. Which sentence uses adjectives and adverbs correctly?
o: After a night of rest, Jordan felt well enough to go to class.
The new graduate handled the emergency calm and careful.
The cafeteria soup tasted differently after the new cook started.
The team did real good on the state safety inspection this year.
E.w: "Well" can be an adjective meaning "in good health," so "felt well" is correct after the linking verb "felt."

n.1: "Calm" and "careful" describe how she handled it, so they modify a verb and must be adverbs: "calmly and carefully."
n.2: "Tasted" is a linking verb here, so it takes an adjective that describes the soup: "tasted different."
n.3: "Did" is an action verb, so it needs the adverb "well"; "real" should also be the adverb "really."

E.q: A student is reviewing the doubling rule, in which stress placement decides whether the final consonant doubles. Which word is spelled correctly?
o: occurence
referrence
openning
referred
E.w: Re-FER is stressed on the last syllable, so the r doubles before -ed: "referred". Doubling depends on where the stress falls in the new word.

n.0: Oc-CUR is stressed on the last syllable, so the r doubles: "occurrence".
n.1: In REF-er-ence the stress moves to the first syllable, so the r does not double: "reference".
n.2: O-pen is stressed on the first syllable, so the n does not double: "opening".

E.q: A charge nurse must tell a coworker that a medication dose was charted at the wrong time. Which sentence has the most appropriate tone?
o: How could you possibly mess up something as basic as charting a dose?
Not to be picky, but charting is kind of a big deal, you know what I mean?
Someone on this shift, and I won't say who, charted a dose at the wrong time.
I noticed the 9 a.m. dose was charted at 11 a.m.; can we fix it together?
E.w: Professional feedback is specific, respectful and focused on solving the problem.

n.0: The scolding question is condescending and likely to make the coworker defensive.
n.1: The passive-aggressive, casual phrasing is vague and unprofessional.
n.2: Hinting instead of speaking directly is indirect and can feel like public blame.

E.q: A patient letter ends by pointing readers to an enclosed report. Which sentence uses parentheses correctly?
o: The results were normal (see the attached report.)
The results were normal. (see the attached report)
The results were normal (see the attached report).
The results were normal, (see the attached report).
E.w: When a parenthetical element ends a sentence but is not a full sentence of its own, the sentence's period goes outside the closing parenthesis.

n.0: The period belongs to the main sentence, so it goes outside the parenthesis.
n.1: A parenthetical that stands as its own sentence must begin with a capital letter and end with its own period inside the parenthesis.
n.3: No comma goes before an opening parenthesis.

E.q: Jordan is drafting the thesis for an argumentative essay on hospital visiting hours. Which qualities would make his thesis statement effective? Select all that apply.
o: It makes a specific claim that a reader could dispute
It is narrow enough to support in the essay's length
It previews the main points the essay will develop
It states a fact that most readers already accept
It poses a question for the essay to explore
It opens with "In this essay, I will discuss"
E.w: An effective thesis is one sentence that states a specific, focused, arguable claim and often previews the main points. It must also be narrow enough to develop fully in the space available.

n.3: A widely accepted fact gives the essay nothing to argue.
n.4: A question is not a thesis; the thesis answers the question with a position.
n.5: An announcement names the topic but takes no position, so it is not a thesis.

E.q: A medical secretary is proofreading a memo that uses the word "however" in several positions. Which sentence contains a comma error?
o: The results were not available, however until Tuesday.
However, the results were not available until Tuesday.
The results, however, were not available until Tuesday.
The results were not available until Tuesday, however.
E.w: "However" used as an interrupter in the middle of a clause must be set off by commas on both sides: "available, however, until Tuesday". One comma is missing.

n.1: Correct: an introductory "However" is followed by a comma.
n.2: Correct: the interrupter is enclosed by a pair of commas.
n.3: Correct: a closing "however" is preceded by a comma.

E.q: A writer wants to turn "The doctor reviewed the X-ray, and she ordered a CT scan" into a simple sentence without changing its meaning. Which revision does this correctly?
o: After the doctor reviewed the X-ray, she ordered a CT scan.
The doctor, who reviewed the X-ray, ordered a CT scan.
The doctor reviewed the X-ray; she ordered a CT scan.
The doctor reviewed the X-ray and ordered a CT scan.
E.w: Removing the second subject (she) leaves one subject with a compound predicate (reviewed ... and ordered): one independent clause, a simple sentence.

n.0: "After the doctor reviewed the X-ray" is a dependent clause, so the result is complex.
n.1: "Who reviewed the X-ray" is a dependent relative clause, so the result is complex.
n.2: A semicolon joining two independent clauses still makes a compound sentence.

E.q: A board member's comment is quoted in a hospital newsletter. Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
o: She called the plan "a good start;" the board disagreed.
She called the plan, "a good start"; the board disagreed.
She called the plan "a good start," the board disagreed.
She called the plan "a good start"; the board disagreed.
E.w: In US style, semicolons and colons go outside the closing quotation mark (only periods and commas go inside).

n.0: A semicolon goes outside the closing quotation mark.
n.1: The quoted words are part of the sentence's structure (the plan is called something), so no comma should introduce them.
n.2: A comma alone between two independent clauses creates a comma splice.

E.q: A hospital's community newsletter is announcing a new screening service. Which sentence uses respectful, person-first language?
o: The clinic now offers free foot exams for people with diabetes.
The clinic now offers free foot exams for diabetics in the area.
The clinic now offers free foot exams for diabetes victims.
The clinic now offers free foot exams for diabetes sufferers.
E.w: Person-first language names the person before the condition: "people with diabetes."

n.1: "Diabetics" labels people by their condition; person-first language puts the person first.
n.2: "Victims" frames people as helpless and defines them by their condition.
n.3: "Sufferers" assumes how people experience the condition and defines them by it.

E.q: A pharmacy student is comparing products in a study guide. Which sentence uses a comparative or superlative form correctly?
o: The night shift is more busier than the day shift on most weekends.
Of the three dressings, the foam one is the least painful to remove.
Of the two inhalers, the blue one is the most effective for her asthma.
Of the three textbooks, this one is the better choice for anatomy.
E.w: With three or more items, use the superlative (-est, most, least). Three dressings are compared, so "least painful" is correct.

n.0: "More busier" is a double comparative; use "busier" alone.
n.2: Comparing exactly two items calls for the comparative: "the more effective."
n.3: Comparing three or more items calls for the superlative: "the best choice."

E.q: Which actions by a student writing a research paper count as plagiarism? Select all that apply.
o: Summarizing a study's findings in her own words with a citation
Stating without a citation that water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit
Submitting a paper written for another course without permission
Paraphrasing an expert's argument without citing the expert
Quoting a nurse's exact words in quotation marks with a citation
Copying a sentence from a website with a citation but no quotation marks
E.w: Plagiarism includes copying exact words without quotation marks (a citation alone does not show the words are copied), using someone's ideas without credit, and reusing your own earlier work without permission.

n.0: A summary in her own words with a citation is correct use of a source.
n.1: The freezing point of water is common knowledge, which needs no citation.
n.4: Exact words in quotation marks with a citation are properly credited.

E.q: A student is labeling word groups taken from a patient education leaflet. Which group of words is a dependent clause?
o: during the long night shift
the nurse finished her charting
running down the hospital hallway
because the pharmacy was closed
E.w: A dependent clause has a subject and a verb (the pharmacy was) but begins with a subordinating conjunction (because), so it cannot stand alone.

n.0: This is a prepositional phrase: it has no subject-verb pair.
n.1: This has a subject and verb and expresses a complete thought, so it is an independent clause.
n.2: This is a participial phrase: "running" is a verbal with no subject.

E.q: Read the paragraph from a clinic flyer. (1) The clinic offers free flu shots. (2) Every Saturday from nine to noon. (3) Patients should bring their insurance cards. (4) Walk-ins are welcome. Which sentence is a fragment?
o: Sentence 1
Sentence 2
Sentence 3
Sentence 4
E.w: Sentence 2 has no subject and no verb; it is a group of prepositional phrases telling when. It could be joined to sentence 1.

n.0: Sentence 1 has a subject (clinic) and a verb (offers) and is complete.
n.2: Sentence 3 has a subject (Patients) and a verb (should bring) and is complete.
n.3: Sentence 4 has a subject (Walk-ins) and a verb (are) and is complete.

E.q: A quality-improvement report summarizes changes in a clinic. Which sentence uses "fewer" or "less" correctly?
o: There were fewer complaints after the new check-in system began.
The new menu offers less calories per serving than the old one did.
The weekend shift now runs with less staff members than before.
The clinic saw less patients this month than it did last month.
E.w: Use "fewer" with countable plural nouns (complaints, patients, calories, staff members) and "less" with uncountable nouns (water, sodium, time).

n.1: "Calories" can be counted, so the sentence needs "fewer calories."
n.2: "Staff members" is a countable plural, so it needs "fewer staff members" ("less staff" alone would be fine).
n.3: "Patients" can be counted, so the sentence needs "fewer patients."

E.q: A charge nurse is reviewing statements in a staff training packet. Which of the following is a complete sentence?
o: The nurse who works nights trained the new aide.
Because the nurse who works nights trained the aide.
Running to the clinic before the nurse's night shift.
The nurse who works nights and trains the new aides.
E.w: "The nurse ... trained the new aide" has a subject (nurse), a main verb (trained) and a complete thought; "who works nights" is a relative clause inside it.

n.1: "Because" makes the whole word group a dependent clause, which cannot stand alone.
n.2: This is a participial phrase with no subject and no main verb.
n.3: The verbs "works" and "trains" both belong to the relative clause beginning with "who", so "The nurse" has no main verb: a fragment.

E.q: Read the sentence: "The nurse carefully explained the very complex procedure." Which word is an adverb that modifies an adjective?
o: complex
explained
very
carefully
E.w: "Very" is an adverb that modifies the adjective "complex", telling how complex the procedure is.

n.0: "Complex" is the adjective being modified; it describes the noun "procedure".
n.1: "Explained" is the verb of the sentence.
n.3: "Carefully" is an adverb, but it modifies the verb "explained", not an adjective.

E.q: Read the sentence: "Before each procedure, staff must ______ every instrument that will touch the patient." Based on its suffix, which word correctly completes the sentence?
o: sterile
sterilize
sterility
sterilely
E.w: The blank follows the helping verb must, so it needs a verb. The suffix -ize forms verbs meaning to make, so sterilize (to make sterile) fits.

n.0: Sterile is an adjective; "must sterile every instrument" has no verb.
n.2: -ity forms a noun (the state of being sterile), which cannot follow must.
n.3: -ly forms an adverb, which describes a verb rather than serving as one.
